tx_new_testament_wall.blurb: New Testament Wall is the right-hand half of the paired Testaments walls on the Medicine Wall limestone band in San Antonio. It is all sport climbing, thirteen routes in total, with a couple of 5.8 warm-ups and then a steady pile of 5.10, 5.11 and 5.12 lines, so it suits people working in the low to mid 5.11 range and up more than newcomers. The base sits right of the trees, and a rock-lined path leads to it from the parking area, passing the neighboring Old Testament Wall on the way. Expect an urban crag with a short walk, and bring a helmet for belaying because loose rock turns up on parts of this cliff band.

tx_old_testament_wall.blurb: Old Testament Wall is the tallest section of the Medicine Wall limestone band in San Antonio, found at the far end of the trail where the cliffs first come into view on your left. It holds thirteen sport routes spread from 5.7 up to 5.11, with plenty of 5.8s and 5.10s, which makes it one of the friendlier sectors for climbers stepping up from easier grades. Quality changes with height: the lower tier has the better rock, while the upper part is chossy and deserves care. A tall orange scar near the top helps you spot the wall. A longer rope helps on the taller lines, and a helmet is a good idea.

tx_morgan_s_point.blurb: Morgan's Point is a small limestone sport crag right at the water's edge on Lake Belton, just west of Temple in central Texas. Its thirteen routes are short, around 25 to 30 feet, and steep. A couple of 5.8s are the only easy options; the rest are mostly 5.11 and 5.12, with one 5.13, so it is a place for people climbing hard rather than a beginner venue. Some lines carry permanent draws. You get a lakeside setting where passing boats often slow down to watch, and the rock is good limestone. It pairs well with other Lake Belton crags on the same trip.

tx_cave_tower.blurb: Cave Tower is the first big tower you meet in the Side Canyons at Lake Mineral Wells State Park, on sandstone bluffs west of the main canyon. A narrow cave tunnels through its middle. The climbing is mostly top-rope, with one sport line and one boulder problem mixed in, and the grades run from an easy 5.5 up through the 5.8 to 5.10 range, making it a good pick for newer climbers and groups. The tower is known for its roofs, and it gets more sun than some neighboring walls. Reach it by descending the stairs from the lot and turning left at the fork. Anchors sit well back from the edge, so bring long slings.

tx_mossy_wall.blurb: Mossy Wall is one of the longer walls at Reimer's Ranch North Shore, near Austin in the Hill Country. All thirteen routes are sport climbs on limestone, concentrated at 5.11 and 5.12 with a single harder line, so it is an area for strong sport climbers. Tufas and caves give the climbing a different feel from the polished rock elsewhere around Austin, and the wall stays in the shade all day, which helps through hot months. Above a loose ledge a dozen or so feet up the rock turns solid. The path in is lightly used and easy to miss, so follow the trail description closely.

tx_gymnasium_the.blurb: The Gymnasium is a bouldering zone on North Mountain at Hueco Tanks, on syenite. It holds a dozen problems, and the spread is gentle compared with much of Hueco: most go at V0 to V3, with several at the very easiest end and only one problem up around V6. That makes it a handy warm-up spot or a place for climbers working through moderate grades. One long traverse links much of the boulder from one side to the other. The area is set up with a north-facing aspect, and the zone feels like a seemingly endless run of problems.

tx_terminator_area.blurb: Terminator Area is a steep bouldering zone on North Mountain at Hueco Tanks. Most of the eleven boulder problems climb out of cave roofs, ranging from V2 up to V10, with a clump in the V4 to V8 band. The syenite boulders face south and the sun is strong, but the caves hold shade over most of the problems, with only the topouts exposed. One 5.12 trad line follows a hand and finger crack across a big roof on the Terminator Boulder; it rarely sees ascents. This area suits strong boulderers who like overhanging power moves.

_skipped.tx_crinoid_cave: private land, search results report climbing closed to the public; the one fetched crag page carries no usable detail and its coordinates are only a best guess
